methodologyNotes: Roster of 13 high-search USB/Thunderbolt audio interfaces for home recording (2014–2024 release years), independently re-verified against manufacturer product/spec pages (focusrite.com, uaudio.com, solidstatelogic.com, presonus.com, audient.com, motu.com, native-instruments.com, behringer.com), major retailers (Sweetwater, Thomann, B&H), and press coverage (Sound on Sound, MusicRadar, AudioXpress, ProSoundWeb). All 13 draft products are real and were retained; no fabrications found. Prices are published US MSRP/MAP where available, else lowest confirmed US street price (noted). Spec-inflation corrected: SSL 2+ MkII inputs corrected from 4 to 2 (manufacturer markets it as 2-in/4-out; the front DI jacks are alternate inputs to the same 2 channels). Behringer UMC22 release year corrected 2013->2014. max_resolution_bit_khz formatted as 'bit-depth / max sample rate kHz'. booleans reflect manufacturer claims (true=yes/included). NOTE on MOTU M2 outputs_analog=4: MOTU markets it as 2x4 counting 2 balanced TRS + 2 RCA jacks, but the RCA pair mirrors the TRS pair (2 unique output channels). Retained 4 to match the manufacturer's physical-jack count. Accessed 2026-06-19.

products.name: Focusrite Scarlett Solo 4th Generation
products.provenance: $159.99 confirmed (Sweetwater/Focusrite US). 1 mic preamp + 1 instrument input (2 analog input jacks), USB-C, 24-bit/192 kHz, bus-powered, no MIDI — confirmed. Released August 2023 (Focusrite 4th Gen launch 24 Aug 2023). Original draft source us.focusrite.com/products/scarlett-solo replaced with live Sweetwater listing.

products.name: Focusrite Scarlett 2i2 4th Generation
products.provenance: $224.99 confirmed (Sweetwater/Focusrite US). 2 mic preamps, USB-C, 24-bit/192 kHz, bus-powered, no MIDI confirmed. Released August 2023 per Sound on Sound and Focusrite. Draft source us.focusrite.com/products/scarlett-2i2 replaced with live Sweetwater listing.

products.name: Focusrite Scarlett 4i4 4th Generation
products.provenance: $299.99 confirmed (Sweetwater/Focusrite US/Crutchfield). 2 mic preamps, 4 analog inputs (2 XLR combo + 2 line), 4 line outputs, USB-C, MIDI In/Out, bus-powered confirmed. Released 2023 (4th Gen lineup). Draft Thomann corroboration replaced with Crutchfield spec page.

products.name: Universal Audio Volt 2 USB Audio Interface
products.priceNote: MSRP at launch; current street price varies
products.provenance: $189 launch MSRP confirmed by MusicRadar Oct 2021 announcement. 2-in/2-out, 24-bit/192 kHz, USB-C, 5-pin MIDI In/Out, bus-powered, 2 mic preamps with Vintage mode confirmed via UA product page. Shipped late November 2021.

products.name: Universal Audio Apollo Twin X DUO Gen 2 (Thunderbolt)
products.provenance: Apollo X Gen 2 series announced 9 Oct 2024 per Sound on Sound. DUO Essentials+ $999 confirmed at Sweetwater (QUAD $1,299). Thunderbolt 3, 2 Unison mic preamps, 24-bit/192 kHz, requires external PSU (not bus-powered), no MIDI. Outputs: 2 monitor + 2 line (ALT) = 4 analog outs. Distinct from the separate 'Apollo Twin X USB' product (July 2024). Draft corroboration replaced Thomann with Sound on Sound announcement.

products.name: PreSonus Studio 24c
products.provenance: $157.99 confirmed directly on PreSonus US product page. 2 XMAX-L mic preamps, USB-C, 24-bit/192 kHz, 5-pin DIN MIDI In/Out, bus-powered, 2-in/2-out confirmed. Announced NAMM 2019.

products.name: Audient iD4 MkII
products.priceNote: Launch US MSRP; street price varies widely ($145 Thomann to ~$269 Sweetwater)
products.provenance: $199 launch MSRP confirmed (announced Jan 2021, available Feb 2021). 1 Class-A console mic preamp, USB-C, 24-bit/96 kHz max (not 192), no MIDI, bus-powered confirmed via Audient spec page and MusicRadar. Current street price spread is wide ($145–$269).

products.name: Audient EVO 4
products.provenance: USB-C, 2-in/2-out, 2 EVO mic preamps, bus-powered, no MIDI, 24-bit/96 kHz confirmed via Audient tech specs. Launched at NAMM 2020. priceUsd corrected $105->$129 to reflect documented US MAP at launch (street ~$99–$160). Draft Musicstore corroboration replaced with Sweetwater listing.

products.name: MOTU M2
products.priceNote: Street price, Sweetwater; MOTU does not publish a separate MSRP
products.provenance: MOTU page confirms 2 mic/line/Hi-Z combo inputs, 2 balanced TRS + 2 RCA outputs (MOTU markets as 2x4; RCA mirrors TRS so 2 unique channels — retained outputs_analog=4 per manufacturer jack count), 24-bit/192 kHz, USB-C, MIDI 5-pin I/O, bus-powered. ~$199.95 at Sweetwater. Released Nov 2019.

products.name: Behringer U-Phoria UMC22
products.priceNote: US street price, Sweetwater (Thomann lists lower, ~$35)
products.provenance: 16-bit/48 kHz confirmed by Thomann spec page (despite some retailer marketing). USB Type-B (USB 2.0), 1 MIDAS-designed mic preamp, bus-powered, no MIDI confirmed. release_year corrected 2013->2014 (manual copyright 2014, NAMM 2014 launch). Price note: Thomann shows ~$35; ~$52.90 reflects US Sweetwater street.

products.name: Solid State Logic SSL 2+ MKII
products.priceNote: US MSRP, confirmed via SSL launch and retailer listings
products.provenance: SSL markets this as a 2-in/4-out interface: 2 mic/line combo inputs (with 2 front Hi-Z DI jacks that share the same 2 channels) and 4 balanced TRS outputs. inputs_analog corrected 4->2 to match SSL's official 2-in spec. 2 SSL preamps, 32-bit/192 kHz, USB-C, 5-pin DIN MIDI I/O, bus-powered confirmed. $299.99 US MSRP. Launched 1 Oct 2024 per SSL/AudioXpress/ProSoundWeb.

products.name: Native Instruments Komplete Audio 2
products.priceNote: List price ~$99–$109; street ~$87–$106; product approaching end-of-life
products.provenance: 2 XLR/TRS combo inputs with preamps, stereo output, 24-bit/192 kHz, USB 2.0 (Type-B micro), bus-powered, no MIDI confirmed via NI spec page and B&H. Launched late 2018 (reviews early 2019). priceUsd set to ~$99 list (street ~$87–$106). Draft source pointed to general product page; replaced with NI specifications page; Musicstore corroboration replaced with B&H.

products.name: MOTU M4
products.priceNote: Street price $277, Thomann USD listing (item 478036); MOTU does not publish a separate MSRP. US retailers (Sweetwater/B&H) were unreachable at access time.
products.provenance: MOTU's official specs page confirms the M4 as a 4-in/4-out USB-C interface: 2 XLR/TRS combo mic/line/Hi-Z inputs (each with independent preamp gain and individual +48V), 2 balanced 1/4-inch line inputs (4 analog inputs total), 4 balanced DC-coupled TRS outputs plus 4 mirrored RCA outputs (4 unique output channels — same jack-count method as the existing M2 entry), 44.1–192 kHz sample rates, USB-C 2.0 bus power, and 1x MIDI IN/OUT. Thomann (item 478036, rated 4.7/5) corroborates the exact M4 model, states the "24 bit / 192 kHz AD/DA converter", lists "Available since November 2019", and shows a $277 USD price. Bit depth (24-bit), release month, and the price come from Thomann because MOTU publishes neither a bit-depth figure nor an MSRP; US retailer pages (Sweetwater, B&H, Guitar Center, Reverb) returned 403/404 at access time.

products.name: Arturia MiniFuse 2
products.priceNote: $249 listed on Arturia official product page (US, arturia.com). Thomann (EU) lists lower converted price ~$122.
products.provenance: Arturia's official MiniFuse 2 product page confirmed model identity (explicitly "MiniFuse 2", distinct from MiniFuse 1/4) and the US price of "249$", plus 2 combo XLR/jack inputs, 2 balanced TRS line outputs, 5-pin MIDI in/out, USB-C, and bus-powered operation. Thomann's retailer page corroborated the full spec set: "24 bit / 192 kHz", 2 mic inputs (dual preamps), 2 line outs, USB Type-C, MIDI I/O, USB bus-powered, and "Available since December 2021" (release date). Both pages agree on every published spec; bit depth (24-bit) is stated verbatim on Thomann.

products.name: Audient iD14 MkII
products.priceNote: Thomann US listing $219 (street price); no manufacturer US MSRP stated on fetched pages. MusicRadar (UK) quotes £200 at launch.
products.provenance: Thomann's iD14 MKII listing (item 510533, "Available since March 2021") confirms the exact model via a full spec table: Connection USB C, 24 bit / 96 kHz, 2 combined mic/line inputs (2 Class-A console mic preamps) plus 1 shared JFET instrument input, 4 line outputs, "MIDI interface: No", and "USB Bus-Powered: Yes"; the price shown is $219. MusicRadar's dated review (7 Sep 2021) independently corroborates a "10-in 6-out, 24-bit 96kHz" bus-powered USB-C unit with two mic/line inputs, one front instrument input "shared with mic/line input 1", and "two pairs of balanced outputs" (= 4 line outs) — so inputs_analog=2 (the DI is an alternate to a mic channel, matching the catalog's SSL 2+ handling). MODEL-IDENTITY NOTE: audient.com's current /id14 page was deliberately NOT used as the source because it now describes a newer 32-bit AD/DA generation (ADC 120 dB / DAC 125.5 dB, with a template error citing "eight" preamps), which differs from the 24-bit/96 kHz MkII (ADC 121 dB / DAC 126 dB); both cited sources here are unambiguously the MkII.

products.name: Universal Audio Volt 276 USB Audio Interface
products.priceNote: Listed at $239 (shown in USD) on the Thomann retailer product page. UA's US store shows "Price displayed at checkout" with no explicit figure, so no manufacturer MSRP could be sourced verbatim; $239 is the only fetched, sourced price figure.
products.provenance: The Universal Audio product page confirms this exact model — "Volt 276 USB Audio Interface", a "Desktop 2-in / 2-out USB audio interface with 2 preamps and class-leading 24-bit / 192 kHz audio conversion", bus-powered via the included USB-C to USB-A cable, with an "onboard 1-in / 1-out MIDI connection" and the 76 Compressor (based on the 1176), distinguishing it from Volt siblings (1/176/2/476/476P/876). Thomann corroborates every spec: 2x2 channels, 2 mic inputs, 2 line outs, Max Resolution 24 bit / 192 kHz, MIDI interface Yes, USB Bus-Powered Yes, Connection Format USB port Type C, and "Available since November 2021" (item 529077). Price: the UA US store shows only "Price displayed at checkout"; the sole sourced figure is Thomann's "$239" (USD), used for priceUsd and noted as such.

products.name: Steinberg UR22C
products.priceNote: $189 as listed in the dated MusicRadar review (published 23 July 2021), which shows the price as £125 / €145 / $189. No live US retailer price was fetchable (Sweetwater, B&H, Reverb, and Perfect Circuit all returned HTTP 403; Vintage King listed the unit as "Product No Longer Available" with no price).
products.provenance: Fetched the official Steinberg UR22C product page as source; it is a JS-rendered SPA (returns only nav/footer text via a clean fetch) but its canonical URL and page title ("UR22C: The Perfect Portable Interface | Steinberg") confirm this exact model. The dated MusicRadar review (corroboration, published 23 July 2021) confirms the UR22C as the entry-level 2-in/2-out UR-C interface: two combination XLR/1/4" D-PRE mic/line inputs, two balanced 1/4" outputs, MIDI In and Out, USB-C (USB 3.1 Gen 1) and 32-bit/192 kHz, and lists the price as $189. A separate Vintage King fetch (MFR# UR22C, "Product No Longer Available") independently corroborated 2 inputs / 2 outputs, 32-bit/192 kHz, XLR combo inputs, 1/4" TRS outputs and MIDI In/Out. Release year is not stated verbatim on the cited pages, so release_year and releaseDate are left null.

products.name: Apogee Duet 3
products.priceNote: US MSRP $649, cited verbatim by Tape Op (Issue #150: "Duet 3 $649 MSRP") and Sound on Sound ("$649"). Retailer street price ~$699 (Chuck Levin's). Apogee's own pages do not publish a price.
products.provenance: Model identity confirmed as the exact Apogee Duet 3: the official Apogee knowledge-base page and Chuck Levin's (Model: DUET-3) both describe a "2x4 USB Type C audio interface" with 2 mic/line + 2 instrument inputs, 2 balanced outputs plus 1/8-inch headphone out, up to 24-bit/192 kHz conversion, up to 65dB preamp gain, bus-powered via USB-C, and no MIDI (the second USB-C port is power-only). Price of $649 US MSRP is stated verbatim by Tape Op (Issue #150, "Duet 3 $649 MSRP") and Sound on Sound ("$649"); Chuck Levin's lists a $699 street price. Apogee markets it as two-in/four-out (the headphone output is independently addressable from the main outs), so outputs_analog=4 is retained per the manufacturer's official 2x4 spec, matching how other entries follow manufacturer output counts. Release year is left null because no fetched page states it verbatim (the SoS review was published April 2022 and the Tape Op review Jul/Aug 2022, both calling it a recent release).
